article_content: The Panama Canal Authority has announced it will further limit the number of ships transiting the canal due to a severe drought worsened by El Niño. This drought, the worst since records began in 1950, has lowered water levels in Gatun Lake, the canal's primary water source. From November 3, daily booking slots will be reduced to 25, and by February 2024, they'll be cut to 18. The Panama Canal is a vital shipping route used by 13,000 to 14,000 ships each year. The restrictions are likely to increase global shipping costs due to delays and reduced availability of vessels.
translated_content: La Autoridad del Canal de Panamá ha anunciado que impondrá más restricciones en el número de barcos que pasan por el canal debido a una sequía severa agravada por El Niño. Desde el 3 de noviembre, se reducirán las reservas diarias a 25, y para febrero de 2024, a 18. El Canal de Panamá es crucial para el comercio global, con entre 13.000 y 14.000 barcos anuales. Se espera que las restricciones aumenten los costos de envío a nivel global por retrasos y menor disponibilidad de buques.

article_content: Florida is facing a significant threat from a large toxic 'red tide', the largest since 2005, as it moves down the coast. The 'red tide', known scientifically as 'Karenia brevis', occurs when microscopic algae blooms surge under the right conditions. It can release harmful chemicals, leading to respiratory issues, and is usually observed in late summer or early autumn. If the 'red tide' approaches within a mile of the beach, the toxins can be released into the air by crashing waves. Don Anderson, a senior scientist at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, noted that these blooms harm wildlife, people, and tourism, and can cause massive fish kills. The current bloom is about 20 miles off Florida's coast, measuring 90 miles in length, 60 miles in width, and at least 100 feet in depth. According to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, approximately 1,000 fish and some crabs and octopi have died so far.

Puede causar problemas respiratorios y suele aparecer a finales del verano o principios del otoño. Si se acerca a la costa, las olas pueden liberar toxinas al aire. Don Anderson, de la Institución Oceanográfica Woods Hole, advierte sobre sus efectos nocivos. La floración actual está a 20 millas de la costa, con dimensiones de 90 millas de largo, 60 millas de ancho y 100 pies de profundidad. Han muerto alrededor de 1,000 peces y otros animales marinos.

article_content: If the first thing you've ever heard about black Jews in Israel came out of the mouth of L.A. Clippers owner Donald Sterling, I'm sorry to hear that. The reported rambling of an octogenarian billionaire in what sounds like a bedroom fight with his mistress probably isn't the best source for dissecting geopolitical religiosity. 'You go to Israel, the blacks are just treated like dogs,' the person who sounds like Sterling said on the recording leaked by somebody, perhaps his mistress. Here's the full exchange: The person: 'It's the world! You go to Israel, the blacks are just treated like dogs.' The mistress: 'So do you have to treat them like that, too?' Person: 'The white Jews, there's white Jews and black Jews. Do you understand?' Mistress: 'And are the black Jews less than the white Jews?' Person: 'A hundred percent, fifty, a hundred percent.' On the surface, Sterling might have a point that dark-skinned Jews have experienced adversity in the Jewish state. But to say 'dogs' isn't quite right. Israel proudly touts successes like Operation Solomon, its airlift of Ethiopian Jews in 1991, where over 14,000 were transported to Israel over 36 hours to escape persecution. There's no question that life is better in the Promised Land. Yet, it hasn't been easy. Ethiopian Jews are among the poorest Israelis, with 72% living below the poverty line. Frustrations boiled over two years ago in Kiryat Malachi, when thousands demonstrated against discriminatory practices. Avishai Mekonen, an Ethiopian Israeli filmmaker, said, 'That's insane. That's disgusting.' He noted that while there are challenges, the community is making progress and has a voice.

Garner, 52, was accused of depraved-heart murder, a charge under Mississippi law indicating a callous disregard for human life. Gordon, 37, travelled from Atlanta, Georgia, to Garner's home in Jackson, Mississippi, for the procedure. Mississippi Attorney General Jim Hood confirmed that Garner lacked the necessary training and license to perform the procedure. Garner was charged with Gordon's death, which occurred several days after the injection in late March 2011. Authorities are investigating whether the implant used was real or counterfeit silicone and are urging other patients treated by Garner to come forward.

article_content: Retired Supreme Court Justice John Paul Stevens has voiced his support for the U.S. operation that killed Osama bin Laden, deeming it legally justified. At Northwestern University, Stevens praised President Barack Obama's decision to authorize the covert mission by U.S. Navy SEALs, citing bin Laden's continuous efforts to attack the U.S. Stevens commended the SEALs, stating, 'I was very proud of the SEALs.' His remarks address the legal debates surrounding the executive's authority to unilaterally decide to kill a terrorist leader without government ties.
translated_content: El ex juez de la Corte Suprema John Paul Stevens ha expresado su apoyo a la operación estadounidense que resultó en la muerte de Osama bin Laden, considerándola legalmente justificada. En Northwestern University, Stevens alabó la decisión del presidente Barack Obama de autorizar la misión secreta de los SEAL de la Marina estadounidense, citando los continuos esfuerzos de bin Laden para atacar a Estados Unidos. Stevens felicitó a los SEAL, diciendo: 'Me sentí muy orgulloso de los SEAL.' Sus declaraciones abordan los debates legales en torno a la autoridad ejecutiva para decidir unilateralmente matar a un líder terrorista sin vínculos con ningún gobierno.
